evidence: On the frozen R15 stock law, both exposed overrun cases reach their maximum precisely on the first detached sample. Before detachment their maximum reaction is below one box weight. The final measured box was still decompressing. This calls for preparing the compliant release state, not detecting a larger touchdown or changing detector thresholds.
law: Only after the incumbent public support/height gate has armed within the final two hybrid blend periods, apply a bounded upward terminal *velocity* to the flange reference. The rise is a quintic velocity blend; target acceleration scale is 5% gravity, with max acceleration below this over the available horizon. Let V=0.5*(0.05*g)*remaining_horizon, hence nominal release lift 0.1962 mm. Return to the unchanged trajectory with position/velocity/acceleration continuity over two incumbent postrelease returns. Do not activate with <one blend period remaining, for zero payload or absent support. Nominal local full-pose Jacobian at release distributes the small translation to all joints; no commanded XY/yaw change. Original task release, time reference and registration, torque and alarm bounds unchanged.
inputs: Encoder, JTS, grip, existing public shared support estimator, known mass/COM, public nominal model and scheduled release. No case ID, pickup offset, actual force, ground-truth box geometry, pulse or trial labels. Post-run force and geometry for diagnosis only.
controls: Compare R10, R15-early, and R16 using exactly the independent staged r16_handoff_check plan. 22 historical original normal cases incl ec1:up/ec3:up and both old failures are exposed; then a disjoint normal matrix and unloaded parity; external impact pairs only after both complete. Retain negative results. No threshold retuning or scenario selection based on holdout. No R10-release change.
